smelter_kazzinc_ukmc.name: Kazzinc Ust-Kamenogorsk Metallurgical Complex (UKMC)
smelter_kazzinc_ukmc.deposit_short_description: The Ust-Kamenogorsk Metallurgical Complex (UKMC) is the flagship integrated zinc-lead-copper-precious metals smelting hub of Kazzinc, Kazakhstan's largest non-ferrous metals producer, in which Glencore plc holds a controlling 69.61% stake. The complex treats polymetallic sphalerite-bearing concentrates from Kazzinc's East Kazakhstan mines and produces roughly 174,000 t zinc, 36,000 t lead and 15,000 t copper plus ~600,000 oz gold in 2023 (Glencore FY2024 production report). Germanium occurs as a trace substituent in the sphalerite feed and concentrates in zinc-plant leach residues and dusts, the classic source from which Ge is recovered as a by-product. Kazzinc/UKMC is treated here as a producing Ge recovery node because the trace-metals circuit handles germanium-bearing intermediates; however, no public figure exists for its germanium output. Successive USGS Minerals Yearbooks for Kazakhstan state that germanium 'may have been produced, but available information was inadequate to make reliable estimates of output,' and neither Kazzinc nor Glencore disclose germanium tonnage in production reports (which itemise only zinc, lead, copper, gold and silver). Reserves of germanium are likewise not separately reported at mine or country level for Kazakhstan. Annual germanium output is therefore recorded as not quantified pending a primary disclosure.

source.name: USGS Minerals Yearbook (Kazakhstan): germanium reserves not reported at mine or country level

refinery_umicore.name: Umicore Germanium Refining & Recycling (Olen / Hoboken)
refinery_umicore.location: Olen and Hoboken, Antwerp Province, Belgium
refinery_umicore.deposit_short_description: Umicore is the leading Western producer and recycler of germanium, refining 6N-7N germanium metal, GeO2, GeCl4 and germanium substrates at its Olen and Hoboken sites in Belgium (with complementary recycling in the U.S.). Independent supply-chain mapping puts Umicore's germanium output at roughly 12-15 t/yr, about 5-7% of global supply (investingermanium.com). Its hydro- and pyro-metallurgical circuits can refine primary feed with Ge concentrations as low as 0.3% and process several thousand tonnes of primary material annually (Umicore). Umicore states that more than 50% of its germanium now comes from recycling (customer scrap, fibre-optic, IR-optics, solar and production scrap), with most of the remaining primary feed drawn from zinc-industry by-products. A strategic new primary source is the DRC: in May 2024 Umicore signed an offtake/processing partnership with Gécamines subsidiary STL covering germanium concentrate recovered from the 'Big Hill' Lubumbashi tailings, with the first 'Made-in-DRC' shipment dispatched to Belgium in October 2024 (Umicore; Gécamines). The Lubumbashi plant is designed to ultimately supply up to ~30% of world germanium demand, with Umicore securing the offtake. Two Umicore germanium recovery/recycling projects (including the GePETO circular initiative) received EU Strategic Project status in 2025. Annual germanium output ~12-15 t/yr.

refinery_ppm_vital.name: PPM Pure Metals / Vital Pure Metal Solutions (Langelsheim)
refinery_ppm_vital.deposit_short_description: The Langelsheim plant in Lower Saxony is a specialist high-purity minor-metals refiner and recycler producing ultra-high-purity germanium (6N grade, resistivity >50 ohm-cm) by reduction of GeO2 to metal followed by zone refining. The site was operated for decades as PPM Pure Metals GmbH (a Recylex group company); on 18 December 2020 China's Vital Materials Co. acquired the PPM Pure Metals industrial site at Langelsheim and now runs it through a newly established subsidiary, Vital Pure Metal Solutions GmbH (VPMS), serving semiconductor, telecom, solar and optoelectronics markets. Independent supply-chain mapping puts germanium output at the site at roughly 2-3 t/yr, about 1% of global supply, drawing on imported concentrates and zone-refined scrap (investingermanium.com). German trade press reports the minor-metals operation is on a growth path. As a producing recycler/refiner, the node feeds refined germanium to the class boundary. Annual germanium output ~2-3 t/yr; no in-ground reserve applies (feed is concentrate and recycling scrap).

dep_almalyk_uztmk.name: Almalyk MMC / UzTMK Germanium (Uzbekistan)
dep_almalyk_uztmk.deposit_short_description: Almalyk Mining and Metallurgical Combine (Almalyk MMC / AGMK), a major Uzbek state-owned copper-zinc-lead-precious metals enterprise, is associated with the country's germanium endowment. Uzbekistan's reported germanium reserve is 74.6 tonnes, cited in an Asian Development Bank-hosted presentation on Uzbekistan's critical minerals potential (Shukurjonov, ADB Asia Clean Energy Forum 2024); other CRM reserves listed include rhenium 804.2 t, tellurium ~2,800 t and indium 38.9 t. Germanium occurs as a trace constituent of sphalerite/polymetallic feed, and Uzbekistan has flagged germanium within a $2.6bn, three-year critical-minerals initiative launched in 2025. However, there is no confirmed current germanium production: the resource is emerging/aspirational and no operating Ge recovery circuit or output figure has been disclosed. The node is therefore TERMINATED (no current germanium output to feed the class boundary). It is retained for the reserve figure (74.6 t) and may be re-activated if Almalyk/UzTMK commissions a germanium recovery line.

smelter_nyrstar_eu.name: Nyrstar EU Germanium Recovery Program (Budel / Balen-Pelt / Auby)
smelter_nyrstar_eu.deposit_short_description: Nyrstar (Trafigura group) has proposed a combined Zinc Critical Minerals Recovery program across its European zinc smelters at Budel (Netherlands), Balen-Pelt (Belgium) and Auby (France) that could produce around 10 tonnes of germanium per year, enough to meet up to 100% of the EU Critical Raw Materials Act's 40% processing benchmark. Germanium is present as a trace constituent in the sphalerite zinc concentrate feed and follows zinc through smelting into intermediate streams from which it could be isolated with dedicated recovery circuits. As of mid-2026 this is a planned program, not an operating germanium line: the projects are under consideration/study and Nyrstar has been seeking policy and investment support. Because there is no current germanium output to feed the class boundary, the node is TERMINATED (outputs empty). Re-activate when a recovery circuit is commissioned and producing.

smelter_nyrstar_hobart.name: Nyrstar Hobart Germanium Scoping
smelter_nyrstar_hobart.deposit_short_description: Nyrstar's Hobart zinc smelter in Tasmania (Trafigura group) is the subject of a government-supported scoping study into recovering critical minerals — germanium and indium — from its zinc circuit. Under an A$135 million Australian Commonwealth/State support package announced for Nyrstar's Hobart and Port Pirie smelters, Nyrstar is to study production of germanium and indium at Hobart (and antimony/bismuth at Port Pirie). Germanium occurs as a trace constituent of the sphalerite zinc concentrate feed and follows zinc into intermediate process streams where, with a dedicated recovery circuit, it could be isolated and refined. This work is at the scoping/feasibility stage only; the funded studies are not expected to deliver definitive answers until late 2026 at the earliest, and no germanium is currently produced. The node is therefore TERMINATED (no current output to feed the class boundary).

source.name: Smelter feed — germanium in sphalerite concentrate, no separate reserve

smelter_boliden.name: Boliden Kokkola / Odda Zinc Smelters (Germanium Feed)
smelter_boliden.deposit_short_description: Boliden operates major European zinc smelters at Kokkola (Finland) and Odda (Norway), both treating sphalerite zinc-sulphide concentrates via direct/oxidative pressure leaching. Rare dispersed metals — gallium, germanium and indium — are present in the sphalerite feed through coupled substitution and report into zinc-plant residues and intermediate streams, so germanium is genuinely contained in Boliden's feedstock. However, there is no confirmed commercial germanium recovery at these sites: published material describes germanium as present in the concentrate, not as a recovered product, and Boliden's own product/operations disclosures cover zinc and other base/precious metals without a germanium output line. Boliden has been expanding zinc capacity (notably Odda, roughly 200 to 350 kt/yr) but no germanium recovery circuit or output figure is confirmed. The node is therefore TERMINATED (recovery unconfirmed, no output to feed the class boundary); re-activate only on a confirmed germanium product disclosure.

company_kazzinc.name: Kazzinc Ltd.
company_kazzinc.description: Kazakhstan's largest zinc, lead and precious-metals producer, controlled by Glencore plc (69.61%); headquartered in Oskemen (Ust-Kamenogorsk). Operates the Ust-Kamenogorsk Metallurgical Complex which in 2023 produced ~173,900 t zinc, 35,600 t lead, 14,800 t copper and ~598,000 oz gold (Glencore FY2024 production report). Germanium is contained in its sphalerite feed and reports to zinc-plant residues, but no germanium output figure is publicly disclosed by Kazzinc or Glencore, and USGS states Kazakhstan's germanium output is inadequate to estimate.

company_glencore.description: Global diversified mining and commodity-trading group; controlling shareholder of Kazzinc (69.61%). Glencore's FY production reports itemise Kazzinc's zinc, lead, copper, gold and silver but do not disclose a germanium output figure.
